request.spec:
A button downloads the pools as a CSV file: a header line pool,member,share,cut then one line per
member, pools in the order added and members in the order added, a pool member as pool:<name>, the
cut as shown (empty when none).

agent.result_text:
There's now an "Export pools (CSV)" button under the Pools panel that downloads the pools as a CSV file. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

- **Format:** the file starts with the header `pool,member,share,cut`, then has one line per member. Pools and their members are in the order they were added. A member that is a pool is written as `pool:<name>`, and the cut is written as the pools list shows it, left empty when there is none. A value containing a comma or a quote is wrapped in quotes, so `Lee, Jo` comes out as `"Lee, Jo"`.
- **It re-reads the pools when you click:** retiring someone doesn't refresh the pools data on screen, so cuts could otherwise be out of date. Because the export re-reads them, a retirement is reflected (Ada's cut drops to 0.00), and the cuts on screen update at the same time.

It's a front-end-only change, in one new file, `src/main/frontend/features/pools/export.slot.tsx`, which follows the existing people export. The server and stored data are unchanged, and the export writes no audit records because the spec doesn't expect any.
